harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Blacklisted the usb-storage kernel module on node1 (CentOS Stream 10) both immediately and persistently across reboot, then verified via the mandatory restart protocol that the block survives a real reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: CentOS Stream 10, kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64, usb_storage not currently loaded
Regenerated initramfs with 'dracut -f --regenerate-all' and confirmed the new image (fresh timestamp) contains no usb_storage reference via lsinitrd
Captured pre-restart baseline boot_id and confirmed config/module state
Triggered 'systemctl reboot' on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Verified boot_id changed (a70d7f83... -> a8628c34...), confirming a real restart occurred
Post-restart verified usb_storage still not loaded and modprobe usb-storage still fails, confirming the blacklist persists across reboot

evidence.summary: Baseline showed module not loaded; blacklist config written; modprobe usb-storage immediately failed with 'could not insert usb_storage: Invalid argument'

evidence.requirement: usb-storage blocked from loading after reboot (persistent)
evidence.summary: initramfs regenerated (fresh timestamp) with no usb_storage reference per lsinitrd; pre-reboot config and unloaded state captured as baseline
Captured boot_id a70d7f83-6867-4c91-851d-7a1228689bb3, blacklist config present, module unloaded

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged (stream closed on disconnect); after polling, node1 responded again with a new boot_id a8628c34-b1a5-40be-873b-a06ab4a0a98b, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery and verification of required state
evidence.summary: After reboot, usb_storage remained unloaded, /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf persisted, and modprobe usb-storage still failed, confirming the blacklist survives reboot

attempts.summary: Blacklisted the usb-storage kernel module on node1 (CentOS Stream 10) both immediately and persistently across reboot, then verified via the mandatory restart protocol that the block survives a real reboot.
